Neural interpretation. Structured computation. Explicit verification.

01 / Mathematics

Symbolic and numerical working.

Composite differentiation, definite integration, matrices and determinants, linear systems, conditional probability, Bayes and selected first-order linear ODEs.

Supported symbolic and numerical results include an explicit check scope.

02 / Physics

Quantities, units and signs.

Charges and electric fields, multi-charge vectors, resistor networks, induction, optics and photoelectric calculations.

Complex tasks may need structured quantities, units and circuit relationships.

03 / Computer science

Bounded, inspectable execution.

Python loops, functions, recursion, exceptions, scope, data structures and stacks; inline CSV analysis; read-only SQL joins, grouping and subqueries.

Arbitrary Python, host files and network access are excluded.

These are small, targeted Class 12-style task families, often using explicit structured inputs. They do not establish complete syllabus mastery, unrestricted natural-language reasoning or new learning by the native Mindscape model.

A little more
about Mindscape.

What is Mindscape, in simple terms?

Imagine teaching someone a board game. You explain the pieces, how they relate, the current position, and the moves allowed. Then you give examples and let them practise. Mindscape explores that idea for AI: provide the structure of a task, learn patterns from examples, and test the actions it takes.

Does it learn differently from other AI?

LLMs learn statistical patterns from large amounts of data, and those patterns can include useful representations of concepts. Mindscape puts an explicit structure around learning: entities, relationships, states, and allowed actions. It combines this structure with learned patterns, memory, and checks. Its coding system currently uses an LLM, so it is a different system design rather than a demonstrated replacement for LLMs. We are testing whether this approach can need fewer examples and produce more reliable results.

What has it been tested on?

The research includes software repair, numerical learning and physical dynamics. The separate Candidate C hybrid scored 36/36 on a targeted STEM hard set and 12/12 on a release holdout. These results measure bounded solver capabilities, not general reasoning or syllabus mastery. See the results and their limits.

Can I use or contribute to Mindscape?

Mindscape is an experimental research project. You can explore the source and reports, or get in touch about collaboration, research support, and ideas.
